This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this project is

A modular R workflow for delineating stream and lake catchments across multiple sites in Canada and computing morphometric metrics. It is project-agnostic: the user supplies a sites table and paths to shared external datasets; the workflow produces self-contained per-site output folders.

All code is plain R scripts sourced interactively — there is no build system, package install step, or test runner. There are no automated tests.

## Running the workflow

The top-level runner is `code/delineate_catchments.R`. It is sourced interactively in R (or run section-by-section), not executed as a CLI script.

```r
# From an R session in the project root:
source("code/delineate_catchments.R")
```

Before running, set the path variables near the top of that file (MRDEM VRT, NHN directory, NHN index shapefile, HydroBasins directory) and define your sites tibble.

To reset outputs selectively before a rerun:

```r
source("code/reset_workflow.R")
reset_site("site_id")          # one site only
reset_group("group_id", sites) # one group cache + its sites
reset_sites(sites)             # all site outputs, keep cache
reset_all()                    # everything
```

To rerun watershed delineation for a single site after editing its pour point in QGIS:

```r
source("R/99_rerun_sites")     # defines rerun_site_watershed()
rerun_site_watershed("site_id", sites, group_manifest, output_dir)
```

## Architecture

### Two-tier processing structure

Processing is split into **groups** (hydrologically coherent regions sharing a DEM) and **sites** (individual pour points). The key insight is that expensive DEM conditioning (breach depressions, flow accumulation) runs once per group, not once per site.

- A **group** is identified by `group_id` in the sites table. All sites sharing a group share a DEM crop and all WhiteboxTools outputs.
- A **site** is a single pour point. Multiple sites can share a group if they fall within the same HydroBasins level-6 polygon(s).

### Module sequence (`R/`)

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `utils.R` | Logging (`cw_inform/warn/abort`), site validation, AOI construction, file-system helpers |
| `01_group_sites.R` | Builds the `group_manifest` sf tibble; creates `cache/<group_id>/` and `output/<site_id>/` directories |
| `02_prepare_dem.R` | Crops MRDEM VRT to each group AOI → `cache/<group_id>/dem.tif` |
| `03_burn_streams.R` | Reads NHN GDB files, merges flowlines/waterbodies, optionally burns streams into DEM → `flowlines.gpkg`, `waterbodies.gpkg`, `dem_burned.tif` |
| `04_run_whitebox.R` | Breach → D8 pointer → accumulation → stream extraction → hillshade → `dem_breached.tif`, `flow_pointer.tif`, `flow_accum.tif`, `streams.tif`, `hillshade.tif` |
| `05_delineate_sites.R` | Snap pour point → watershed delineation → polygon conversion → clip all group rasters to each catchment → per-site outputs |
| `06_remove_upstream.R` | For nested sites: erases smaller upstream catchments from larger downstream ones → `catchment_clipped.gpkg` |
| `07_reclip_outputs.R` | Re-clips all rasters and flowlines to the clipped catchment polygon → `*_clipped.tif` / `streams_clipped.gpkg` |
| `06_catchment_metrics.R` / `08_catchment_metrics.R` | Computes geometry, areal, and relief morphometric metrics following Shekar & Mathew (2024). `08_` computes both unclipped and clipped versions. |

### The `group_manifest` object

This sf tibble is the central data structure passed between modules. One row per group; columns: `group_id`, `burn_streams`, `buffer_m`, `aoi` (sfc geometry in EPSG:3979), `cache_dir`, `n_sites`. It is built by `build_group_manifest()` in Stage 1 and passed to every downstream stage.

### Caching

Every output file is checked with `cache_exists(path)` before writing. Re-running the workflow safely skips completed steps. To force a rerun, delete the relevant file or use the `reset_*()` helpers.

### CRS

All spatial outputs are in **EPSG:3979** (Canada Atlas Lambert NAD83(CSRS)), matching the MRDEM native CRS. No reprojection occurs in normal use.

### External data (not in repo)

| Dataset | Description |
|---|---|
| MRDEM `.vrt` | 30 m national DEM, streamed via VRT — no tile downloads |
| NHN GDB files | National Hydro Network per NTS sheet (`nhn_rhn_<sheet>_gdb_en/`) |
| NHN index shapefile | `NHN_INDEX_WORKUNIT_LIMIT_2.shp` — maps sheet codes to geometries |
| HydroBasins | `north_america/` and `arctic/` subdirectories, levels 1–12 `.shp` |

On Sam's machine these live under `~/Documents/cfs/shared_data/raw/`.

### Pour point correction

When a catchment looks wrong, the pour point snapped to the wrong stream cell. The fix:

1. Open `output/<site_id>/pour_point_snapped.shp` and `streams_tmp.tif` in QGIS
2. Edit `pour_point_snapped.shp` to move the point to the correct stream cell
3. Run `rerun_site_watershed()` (see above) — it reads the edited `.shp` directly without rerunning snapping

### Key design decisions

- **DEM is written as a rectangular crop, not masked to the AOI polygon.** Masking introduces NoData at AOI edges, which prevents WhiteboxTools from computing flow direction for those cells and produces incorrect catchments near the boundary.
- **`burn_streams` is a group-level flag**, not per-site. All sites in a group must share the same value.
- **HydroBasins region (na vs ar)** is resolved spatially by intersection with level-1 boundaries, not by latitude threshold.
- **`99_rerun_sites`** is a script (no `.R` extension) that defines `rerun_site_watershed()` for fixing individual sites post-delineation without clearing the full group cache.

# Catchment Workflow — Project Context

## Project overview
Reproducible R workflow to characterise lake and river catchments for water
quality modelling of post-industrial vegetation recovery in Sudbury, Ontario.
Two study systems: CAM lakes (45 sites) and CELESTE/river sites.

## Project structure
- `workflow/run_cam_lakes.R`                    — ACTIVE top-level runner (Stages 1–7)
- `workflow/R/lake/05_hydroweight_attributes.R` — ACTIVE hydroweight module (Stage 7)
- `cam_workflow_lake.R`        — superseded by workflow/run_cam_lakes.R
- `upstream_clipping_lake.R`   — superseded by workflow/R/lake/04_remove_upstream_lakes.R
- `hydroweight_cam_canlcc.R`   — superseded by workflow/R/lake/05_hydroweight_attributes.R
- `hydroweight_debug.R`        — Diagnostic script for hydroweight
- `05_delineate_sites.R`       — River site delineation
- `06_remove_upstream.R`       — River upstream clipping
- `07_reclip_outputs.R`        — River reclip outputs to clipped catchment
- `08_catchment_metrics.R`     — Morphometric metrics (clipped + unclipped)
- `cam_workflow.R`             — SUPERSEDED point-based version, do not use
- `upstream_clipping.R`        — SUPERSEDED, do not use
- `hydroweight_cam.R`          — SUPERSEDED OLCC version, do not use
- `upstream_network_test.R`    — Experimental, abandoned

## CRS
EPSG:3161 (NAD83 / Ontario MNR Lambert) throughout — OIH native CRS.
Never reproject rasters during analysis.

## Key decisions
- Flow direction: OIH Enhanced Flow Direction recoded to Whitebox encoding
  (one-step clockwise rotation: OIH 128→WBT 1, 1→2, 2→4, 4→8, 8→16, 16→32, 32→64, 64→128)
- Pour points: buffered lake polygon (30 m) rasterized to FULL D8 extent (no trim before wbt_watershed)
- Upstream area threshold: 4 ha minimum based on OIH lake polygon area (not catchment area)
- Excluded waterbody types: Pond
- CANLCC is reprojected once to EPSG:3161 and cached to cache/CAM/hydroweight_loi/canlcc_reprojected.tif
  by prepare_loi_layers() in 05_hydroweight_attributes.R (terra temp file GC avoidance)
- Stream rasters passed to hydroweight() as target_S are extended to the full DEM extent
  via terra::extend() so flow-path distances can be computed across the entire catchment domain

## R style preferences
- tidyverse style with native pipe |>
- Well-commented for reproducibility
- Section headings use ---- style (RStudio/Positron outline compatible)
- PROJECT_ID namespaces all output/cache paths
